FOREWORD

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Travel, Tourism, and Hospitality Related Services Sectional Committee had been approved by the Service Sector Division Council.

Exhibitions play an important role in boosting economic growth, encouraging innovation, and supporting product development across various industries. It also plays a significant role to promote trade, promoting innovation, supporting industry collaboration, and enhancing consumer engagement. As the scale and complexity of exhibitions continue to grow, there is an increasing need for a structured, consistent, and safety oriented approach to their planning and execution. Additionally, exhibitions also contribute to regional economic development by promoting tourism, hospitality, logistics, and allied service sectors.

This standard has been developed to provide comprehensive requirements and recommendations for organizing exhibitions. It covers key aspects, including venue selection, infrastructure planning, operational coordination, safety and security management, emergency preparedness, and post-event evaluation and site clearance. By establishing clear expectations and uniform processes, the standard aims to enhance the quality, reliability, and overall experience for exhibitors, visitors, stakeholders, and supporting agencies.

The objective of this standard is to support exhibition organizers, exhibitors, and service providers in adopting a systematic approach that will contribute to improving operational efficiency, enhancing risk management, and the promotion of best practices across the exhibition sector.

The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex D.

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.




Indian Standard ORGANIZATION OF EXHIBITION — REQUIREMENTS AND


RECOMMENDATIONS


## 1 SCOPE

This standard specifies the requirements and provides recommendations for exhibition organizers and service providers involved in planning, setup, and operation in organizing exhibition.

The standard covers the key aspects for organizing an exhibition including venue selection, infrastructure planning, safety, security, and emergency preparedness, and post-event evaluation and site clearance.

## 3 TERMINOLOGY

In addition to the definitions given in IS/ISO 25639-1 and IS/ISO 37500, the following definitions shall apply.


### 3.1  Attendee — An individual attending an

exhibition including visitor, exhibitor staff, speaker, delegate, media representative and any other verified admission category.

NOTE — Attendee does not include staff of the organizer and the service provider.


### 3.2  Booth — Structure or space occupied for the display of products or services.


### 3.3  Booth Space — Area indoors and/or outdoors, occupied and contracted by an exhibitor whether paid or unpaid, for the display of products or services.


3.4  Exhibition — An event in which products, services, or information are displayed and disseminated.

NOTE — The term exhibition excludes flea market and street market.


### 3.5  Exhibitor — Any organization or individual taking the space/stall on rent in the exhibition from the exhibition organizer.


### 3.6  Exhibition Manual — An electronic or physical document containing event information, rules and regulations, plans, and other information pertinent to exhibitors.


3.7  Exhibition Venue — Designated physical premises where an exhibition is organized.


### 3.8  Exhibition Organizer — An entity that is responsible to produce and manage the exhibition.

## 5 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS


### 5.1  Statutory and Regulatory Requirements

Exhibition organizers shall comply with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, including obtaining permissions from local authorities to host an exhibition such as ‘No Objection Certificate (NOC)’ from the fire department, police permission, approvals from local government bodies, and liquor license, wherever required. The exhibition organizer shall display all such approvals and permissions at a prominent place at the venue in an accessible format.


### 5.2  Identification and Mitigation of Risk

The exhibition organizer shall conduct a risk assessment to identify potential risks associated with organizing the exhibition. The exhibition organizer shall ensure that:

- a) All areas and sources of uncertainty that may affect exhibitors, the venue, attendees, and visitors shall be analysed;
- b) Physical surveys at the venue are conducted to identify the on-ground risks involved;
- c) The results of the risk identification analysis shall be recorded as a list of identified risks, their causes and potential consequences;
- d) A documented mitigation plan shall be prepared and implemented by the exhibition organizer; and




- e) The records of the risk assessment and mitigation plan shall be maintained.

## 7 INFRASTRUCTURE REQUIREMENTS

The exhibition organizer shall identify, plan and ensure the availability of all necessary infrastructure required for organizing an exhibition.


### 7.1  Carpets

Carpets used at the exhibition venue (both indoor and outdoor) shall comply with the following requirements:

- a) The quality of carpets shall be suitable for their intended purpose. The thickness and condition (new or reusable) shall be determined by the exhibition organizer based on the nature, requirements and suitability of the exhibition;
- b) Carpets shall be laid by trained and skilled personnel using appropriate tools and techniques;
- c) Carpets shall be securely fixed using double sided tape or any other suitable material to ensure safety and stability; and
- d) Carpeted areas shall be regularly inspected to ensure cleanliness and maintenance, and any damaged sections shall be promptly repaired or replaced during the exhibition.

### 8.2 Logistics Services

The exhibition organizer shall ensure effective logistics planning and coordination to facilitate the organized movement of materials, exhibits, and supplies. The exhibition organizer shall ensure the following:

- a) Logistics operations including loading, unloading, and internal movement of exhibition materials, exhibits and other supplies are carried out in an organized manner;
- b) Dedicated entry and exit points are designated for logistics movement; and
- c) Scheduling and allocation of time slots are followed for exhibitor setup, dismantling and material handling.
NOTES


1 Additional logistics equipment should be available on site to meet any emergency or breakdown situations.


2 Temporary storage facilities, if required, should be clearly demarcated, monitored, and managed by authorized personnel.


### 8.3  Housekeeping Services

The exhibition organizer shall deploy adequate housekeeping staff throughout the venue to maintain cleanliness and hygiene. The exhibition organizer shall:

- a) prepare the cleaning and hygiene management plan for the exhibition venue;
- b) ensure that cleaning staff are adequately trained and equipped with suitable tools, cleaning materials and personal protective equipment (PPE), as necessary;
- c) maintain, review and retain records of cleaning activities on daily basis; and
- d) cleaning personnel shall follow a prescribed dress code for easy identification and accountability.
NOTE — The exhibition organizer may engage external agency to handle housekeeping services (partially or fully) as per the established plan, however, designated person should monitor the housekeeping activities.

### 8.4  Food and Beverages Services

The exhibition organizer shall ensure:

- a) compliance with food safety regulations and hygiene standards, as applicable;
- b) availability of clean, and well equipped food and beverage service areas for visitors, exhibitors and staff;
- c) sufficient seating arrangements and waste disposal bins;
- d) availability of hand washing facilities near the food service area; and
- e) regular inspection and monitoring of food service operations to ensure hygiene, and waste management.

### 8.5  Waste Management and Sanitation Service

The exhibition organizer shall establish, document and implement a waste management plan covering waste collection, segregation, recycling, and disposal in accordance with local municipal and environmental regulations. The exhibition organizer shall ensure the following measures, including but not limited to:

- a) Placement of waste bins strategically across the venue, clearly labelled for biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste;
- b) Collection and removal of waste at regular intervals to prevent littering;
- c) Coordination with authorized waste collection and disposal agencies to ensure timely removal of waste; and
- d) Periodic inspection to verify compliance with the waste management plan.

## 9 OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS

The exhibition organizer shall ensure that all operations are carried out in a systematic, safe and timely manner in compliance with applicable regulatory requirements. All operational activities shall be planned, coordinated, and monitored to ensure efficiency, visitor comfort, and overall safety during the event.


### 9.1  Booth Contractor

The exhibition organizer shall appoint official booth contractors for construction, setup, and dismantling of exhibition booths. The exhibitor may also appoint the booth contractor of their choice as per the exhibition manual. The booth contractor shall be responsible for, including but not limited to, the following:

- a) Construction, setup, and dismantling of
exhibition booths within the timeframe provided by the exhibition organizer/exhibitor;

- b) Inspecting booth structures for safety and
compliance before opening to visitors; and

- c) Maintaining coordination among the exhibition organizer, contractors, exhibitors and logistics service providers for timely completion of setup activities.

### 9.2  Registration

The exhibition organizer shall establish a registration process for visitors, which may be conducted through online or onsite modes. The exhibition organizer shall:

- a) establish and implement registration process;
- b) mark the registration area and deploy an appropriate number of designated and trained personnel to handle visitor volumes;
- c) display signage to guide visitors toward registration areas with multilingual support;
- d) establish a sufficient number of registration counters, including separate counters for persons with special needs and senior citizens; and
- e) issue badges, passes, or wristbands to all registered visitors.
NOTES


1 In case of high visitors traffic, additional dedicated registration counters for individuals with special needs, senior citizens and children should be established.


2 Self-service kiosks should be deployed for quick check-in and on-site registrations, if needed.


3 Advanced ticketing or registration systems should be utilized.


### 9.3  Help Desk and Information Counter

The exhibition organizer shall set up help desks and information counters at strategic points across the venue to assist visitors with directions, schedules, and general inquiries. The exhibition organizer shall:

- a) employ trained personnel familiar with the event layout, exhibitor locations, and emergency procedures;
- b) provide digital information kiosks and maps to supplement physical counters and enhance visitor accessibility;
- c) display contact details of organizers, emergency services, and lost-and-found at all help desks; and
- d) monitor visitor inflow/outflow to ensure there is no overcrowding inside venue.

### 9.4 Role and Responsibilities

The exhibition organizer shall define the roles and responsibilities for personnel involved in organizing of the exhibition, including event management teams, security staff, housekeeping, logistics, and emergency services. The exhibition organizer shall:

- a) establish a communication hierarchy to facilitate quick decision making and issue resolution;
- b) brief all officials and staff on their assigned duties and operational procedures;
- c) provide adequate training to all staff members; and
- d) conduct periodic briefings and orientation sessions to ensure uniform understanding of procedures.

### 9.5 Safety and Security

The exhibition organizer shall establish and implement a security plan and deploy adequate trained security personnel for visitor management, surveillance and protection of exhibition property. The exhibition organizer shall:

- a) demarcate and monitor security checkpoints and restricted zones through CCTV systems;
- b) ensure availability and functionality of security equipment; and




- c) brief security personnel on their duties, emergency evacuation procedures, and coordination with local authorities

### 9.6  Temporary Manpower

The exhibition organizer shall:

- a) deploy temporary manpower, depending on operational needs such as visitor assistance, logistic support, ticketing and other general operational activities;
- b) ensure temporary staff are adequately trained for their assigned duties and supervised; and
- c) issue identification badges or uniforms for easy recognition.

### 9.7  Fire Safety and Emergency Preparedness

The exhibition organizer shall ensure that the exhibition venue is equipped with adequate fire safety measures, including fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, alarm systems, and emergency exits. The exhibition organizer shall ensure that:

- a) all firefighting equipment are inspected and certified by appropriate authorities prior to commencement of the event;
- b) no flammable materials, open flames, or hazardous substances are used by booth contractors and exhibitors without prior approval;
- c) emergency response and evacuation plans are displayed at key points and communicated to all staff and exhibitors;
- d) a mock drill or orientation session on emergency procedures is conducted prior to the exhibition opening; and
- e) all fire safety equipment and devices used are BIS certified, where applicable.
NOTE — For further guidance on fire safety, the National Building Code, SP 7 : 2016 may be referred.


### 9.8  Visitor Management

The exhibition organizer shall prepare and establish a visitor management plan covering entry points,

registration, visitor flow and exit points. The exhibition organizer shall:

- a) clearly define entry and exit points with proper signage and queue management system;
- b) maintain records of visitor data, including attendance statistics for post event analysis and feedback; and
- c) utilize real-time monitoring through digital systems, where feasible, to manage visitor density and prevent overcrowding;

### 9.9  Post Event Dismantling and Site Clearance

The exhibition organizer shall ensure that post-event dismantling is carried out in an orderly manner under the supervision of the designated official(s). The exhibition organizer shall ensure:

- a) all booth materials, temporary structures,
and promotional displays are removed within the timeframe specified in the event plan;

- b) safe removal of electrical connections and
disposal of waste materials in accordance with waste management plan and environmental guidelines; and

- c) confirmation and documentation of restoration of the venue.

## 10 SUSTAINABILITY

The exhibition organizer shall integrate sustainability principles into all stages of exhibition planning, execution and post-event activities. Measures shall be adopted to minimize environmental impact, optimize resource utilization, and promote responsible practices among all stakeholders. The exhibition organizer shall consider the following:

- a) Waste Management — The waste management plan shall be established, documented, and implemented. Waste shall be segregated at source into dry and wet categories and disposed of in accordance with applicable municipal and environmental regulations. Attendees shall be encouraged to use waste bins through visible signage;
- b) Energy Conservation — The exhibition organizer shall adopt measures to promote energy efficiency, including but not limited to, the following:
- 1) Use of energy efficient lighting systems, equipment, and appliances; and



- 2) Ensuring that all electrical devices and installations are switched off during non-operational hours or when not needed.
- c) Use of Environment-Friendly Materials — To the extent possible, the material used for booth construction, decoration and promotional activities shall be environment friendly and recyclable such as bagasse, bamboo, palm leaves, paper and cardboard;
- d) Digital Documentation — The exhibition organizer should promote the use of digital alternatives including electronic tickets, e-brochures, digital signage, and interactive screens. All communication, including exhibitor information, event schedules, and announcements, shall preferably be shared through electronic means;

## 11 CUSTOMER FEEDBACK

The exhibition organizer shall establish and implement a feedback mechanism to ensure continuous improvement in service quality and visitor experience. The exhibition organizer shall:

- a) provide accessible channels (physical,
digital, or online) for exhibitors and visitors to submit feedback;

- b) prepare and obtain feedback in the
structured format;

- c) monitor, record, and respond to feedback in
a timely and transparent manner; and

- d) analyse feedback to identify strengths,
areas for improvement, and corrective actions for future events.


## 12 BIS CERTIFICATION MARKING

The service(s) conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products may be marked with the Standard Mark.

## ANNEX C

(Clause 6.6)

(Normative)

SAFETY AND EMERGENCY PLAN

C-1 SAFETY AND EMERGENCY PLAN ELEMENTS

The safety and emergency plan shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

- a) Identification and assessment of potential hazards and risks associated with the exhibition venue;
- b) Fire safety arrangements, including the installation of firefighting equipment, fire exits, and evacuation routes;
- c) Medical emergency procedures, including the availability of first-aid facilities, ambulance services, and contact details of nearby hospitals.
- d) Emergency response procedures for incidents such as fire, electrical faults,
equipment failure, accidents, or natural disasters.

- e) Clear signage for evacuation routes;
- f) Training of personnel responsible for handling specific types of emergencies;
- g) Regular safety briefings and drills for staff, exhibitors, and service providers; and
- h) Coordination with local authorities such as fire, police, and medical services for timely assistance during emergencies.
